--- title: "Python in a post" description: "Running Python when the post is rendered: figures, tables and numbers in the text that come straight from the data." author: "Tolborg Group" date: 2026-11-05 categories: [guide, python] --- A code block written as ```` ```{python} ```` is *run* when the post is rendered, and whatever it prints or plots ends up in the post. This means that the figures and numbers in a post are made from the data, rather than copied in by hand, and that they are updated when the data changes. The example here is a $k$-point convergence test of a total energy, stored as `kpoint-convergence.csv` next to this post. ## Reading the data ::: {#7cc81663 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import pandas as pd df = pd.read_csv("kpoint-convergence.csv") df.head() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html}
k_per_side energy_ev
0 2 -4.422
1 3 -4.651
2 4 -4.751
3 5 -4.812
4 6 -4.847
``` ::: ::: The code runs in the post's folder, so files next to `index.qmd` are read by their name. The last expression of a block is displayed, as in a Jupyter notebook, and a data frame is shown as a table. ## Options for a code block Lines at the top of a block starting with `#|` are *cell options*. They set how the block and its output are shown, e.g. a label and caption that turn the output into a numbered table: ::: {#tbl-convergence .cell tbl-cap='Total energy relative to the finest mesh.' execution_count=2} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}
k-points per side Energy (eV) Error (meV)
2 -4.422 450.000
3 -4.651 221.000
4 -4.751 121.000
5 -4.812 60.000
6 -4.847 25.000
7 -4.859 13.000
8 -4.864 8.000
10 -4.868 4.000
12 -4.872 0.000
``` ::: ::: `echo: false` hides the code and keeps the output, which is what most posts want for most blocks. Other useful options are `code-fold: true`, which hides the code behind a "Code" toggle, as in the block below, and `output: false`, which runs the code without showing anything. ## Figures A plot made with Matplotlib becomes a figure, and with a `fig-` label it can be referred to as @fig-convergence. ::: {#cell-fig-convergence .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code code-fold="true"} import matplotlib.pyplot as plt fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 3.5)) ax.plot( df["k_per_side"], df["energy_ev"], "o-", color="#0f766e", markerfacecolor="white", markeredgewidth=1.5, ) ax.axhline(E_ref, color="gray", linewidth=0.8, linestyle="--") ax.set_xlabel("$k$-points per side") ax.set_ylabel("Total energy (eV)") ax.set_xticks(df["k_per_side"]) ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False) plt.show() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![Convergence of the total energy with the number of $k$-points per side. The dashed line is the value for the finest mesh.](index_files/figure-html/fig-convergence-output-1.png){#fig-convergence width=527 height=324} ::: ::: ## Numbers in the text A value computed in a block can be written straight into a sentence with inline code that starts with `python` in braces, as shown below the following block: The energy is converged to within 5 meV from 10 $k$-points per side, as seen in @tbl-convergence. Written in the source, that sentence is ```markdown The energy is converged to within `{{python}} tolerance_mev` meV from `{{python}} k_converged` $k$-points per side, as seen in @tbl-convergence. ``` so changing the tolerance, or the data, changes the text with it. ## When is the code run? The blog is set up with `freeze: auto` in `_quarto.yml`. A post's code is run when the post is rendered for the first time and again only when its `index.qmd` changes. The results are stored in the `_freeze/` folder, which is committed together with the post. This has two advantages: - Old posts keep working even if the code or data they used has moved on. - A post can use data that is too large for the repository, or computations that only run on the cluster: as long as `_freeze/` is committed, GitHub only needs the stored results to publish the blog. ::: {.callout-important} Remember to commit `_freeze/` together with the post. If the stored results are missing, the post is run again when the blog is published, which fails if the data is not in the repository. ::: ## Packages The code runs in the Pixi environment of the blog. A package that a post needs is added with ```bash pixi add scipy ``` and the updated `pixi.toml` and `pixi.lock` are committed with the post.
